items.definition: A chemical messenger produced by a gland and carried in the blood to a target organ where it produces an effect.
items.sentence: Insulin is a [blank] produced by the pancreas that lowers blood glucose levels.

items.definition: A hormone produced by the pancreas that causes cells to take up glucose from the blood, lowering blood sugar levels.
items.sentence: [Blank] is released after a meal to lower the level of glucose in the blood.

items.definition: A hormone produced by the pancreas that causes the liver to convert glycogen into glucose, raising blood sugar levels.
items.sentence: [Blank] is released when blood glucose is too low, causing the liver to release more glucose.

items.definition: A hormone produced by the adrenal glands in response to stress or danger, preparing the body for 'fight or flight'.
items.sentence: [Blank] increases heart rate and breathing rate to prepare the body for sudden action.

items.definition: A female sex hormone produced by the ovaries that controls the development of secondary sexual characteristics and the menstrual cycle.
items.sentence: [Blank] is responsible for the development of female secondary sexual characteristics during puberty.

items.definition: A male sex hormone produced by the testes that controls the development of male secondary sexual characteristics.
items.sentence: [Blank] is produced by the testes and causes voice-breaking and increased muscle mass in males.

items.definition: A hormone produced by the thyroid gland that regulates the metabolic rate of the body.
items.sentence: [Blank] controls the speed of chemical reactions in the body and is important for normal growth.

items.definition: The gland that produces insulin and glucagon to regulate blood glucose levels.
items.sentence: The [blank] monitors blood glucose levels and releases insulin or glucagon to maintain balance.

items.definition: A condition in which the body cannot regulate blood glucose levels properly; Type 1 is caused by lack of insulin, Type 2 by insensitivity to it.
items.sentence: People with Type 1 [blank] cannot produce insulin and must inject it to control blood sugar.

items.definition: The maintenance of a constant internal environment within the body, despite external changes.
items.sentence: The control of blood glucose and body temperature are both examples of [blank].

items.definition: A control mechanism in which a change triggers a response that reverses the change, maintaining a steady state.
items.sentence: [Blank] ensures that blood glucose levels return to normal after a meal.

items.definition: The period of physical development during which the body matures and becomes capable of reproduction.
items.sentence: Sex hormones such as oestrogen and testosterone cause the changes associated with [blank].

items.definition: The monthly cycle of hormonal changes in females that prepares the uterus for pregnancy.
items.sentence: The [blank] is controlled by the hormones FSH, LH, oestrogen, and progesterone.

items.definition: Follicle Stimulating Hormone; a hormone that stimulates the ovaries to produce oestrogen and causes an egg to mature.
items.sentence: [Blank] is released by the pituitary gland and causes an egg follicle to develop in the ovary.

items.definition: Luteinising Hormone; the hormone that triggers ovulation (the release of an egg from the ovary).
items.sentence: [Blank] causes ovulation by triggering the release of a mature egg from the ovary.

items.definition: Anti-Diuretic Hormone; a hormone produced by the pituitary gland that controls water reabsorption in the kidneys.
items.sentence: [Blank] causes the kidneys to reabsorb more water when the blood becomes too concentrated.

items.definition: The master gland in the brain that releases several hormones including FSH, LH, and ADH.
items.sentence: The [blank] gland is sometimes called the master gland because it controls many other endocrine glands.

items.definition: The storage form of glucose found in the liver and muscles, which can be converted back to glucose when needed.
items.sentence: Excess glucose is converted to [blank] for storage in the liver.

items.definition: Methods used to prevent pregnancy, some of which use synthetic hormones to alter the menstrual cycle.
items.sentence: Hormonal [blank] uses oestrogen and progesterone to prevent the release of eggs.

items.definition: The specific organ that a hormone travels to in the blood and causes a response in.
items.sentence: The liver is the [blank] for glucagon, responding by breaking down glycogen into glucose.
